title: Remove One Element to Make the Array Strictly Increasing
summary: Determine if the given 0-indexed integer array nums can be made strictly increasing by removing exactly one element, or if it is already strictly increasing.
statement: Determine if the given 0-indexed integer array nums can be made strictly increasing by removing exactly one element, or if it is already strictly increasing. An array is considered strictly increasing if each element is greater than the previous one (i.e., nums[i - 1] < nums[i] for all 1 <= i < nums.length). Return true if the condition is met, otherwise return false.
constraints: The remaining sequence must be strictly increasing.
Return true when the input already qualifies or can qualify after removing at most one element.
hints: Only the first non-increasing adjacent pair can require a removal.
Try omitting either endpoint of that pair and scan the remainder for strict increase.
If the array has no violation, either check already succeeds.
Any one-element repair must remove an endpoint of the first violation, so the two checks are exhaustive and sufficient.
editorial: Any one-element repair must remove an endpoint of the first violation, so the two checks are exhaustive and sufficient.

tests.explanation: Removing ten leaves 1,2,5,7, which is strictly increasing.
Removing either side of the first violation still leaves another violation.
